definition: Erotica refers to sexually arousing visual content. In this context, it is an example of engaging emotional material that can hold attention and make it slower to shift gaze away.

reasons: The packet only uses “erotica” as an example of an engaging picture content; it does not define the term as sexually arousing visual content.
The second sentence overgeneralizes by turning the article’s specific finding about arousing scenes and saccade slowing into a broad definition of erotica as emotional material that holds attention.
The packet does not define “erotica” as “sexually arousing visual content,” nor does it explicitly state the sexual-arousal meaning of the term.

The claim that erotica is “an example of engaging emotional material” and that it can make it slower to shift gaze away is broadly supported by the packet’s statement that ocular disengagement is affected by engaging picture contents “such as erotica,” along with findings of delayed saccade initiation from emotional (arousing) scenes. However, because the sexual-arousal definition is not supported, the definition cannot be accepted as written.
